newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam Buddhist church denies protest report.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam Buddhist church denies protest report.

text.p: The state-sponsored Vietnam Buddhist Church on Wednesday denied a report that two of its leading monks had resigned from their posts in protest over government interference in religious affairs.

A VBC official in Ho Chi Minh City dubbed the report, by the Paris-based International Buddhist Information Bureau, "idle talk" and said it stemmed from a minor disagreement over church leadership in the central highlands province of Lam Dong.
"It's just an administrative issue before the selection of personnel," said the official, who declined to be named.

The Buddhist Watchdog group said in a statement that Thich Tu Man and Thich Tam Thanh had quit as chairman and vice-chairman of Lam Dong VBC's provincial executive committee after security forces arrested a superior monk and destroyed his pagoda.

"Their resignation followed a government clampdown against Buddhists in Lam Dong province in which security police arrested Thich Minh Dao...superior monk of Long Tho Pagoda near Dalat, expelled 34 resident monks and nuns and subsequently razed the pagoda's 15 buildings to the ground," it said.
It added that Man, as local VBC chairman, had been forced by the authorities to sign a letter denouncing the pagoda's monk and calling for him to be "punished according to the law".
Last month, Vietnam's Foreign Ministry dismissed a previous report by the International Buddhist Information Bureau on what happened to the pagoda and its superior monk.

"In fact there is no such thing as the Long Tho pagoda Zen meditation centre," a ministry spokesman said, adding that the man arrested had pretended to be a monk, occupied public land, duped and deluded people and sexually abused women.
The watchdog said the resignations were another example of growing discontent among VBC dignitaries, many of whom were formerly members of the now-outlawed Unified Buddhist Church of Vietnam (UBCV).

The UBCV was the Buddhist church in former South Vietnam until the victory of Hanoi's communist forces over the south in 1975. Many Buddhists in the south, who were forced to join the VBC after it was set up in 1981, and even more who live abroad, still regard the UBCV as the sole legitimate church organisation in Vietnam.

The International Buddhist Information Bureau also said that a UBCV monk was released from prison last month after serving a four-year sentence for his involvement in a 40,000-strong Buddhist demonstration in the central city of Hue in 1993.

The group said it was not known if the monk, Thich Hai Tang, would be allowed to return to resume his functions at the Linh Mu pagoda, a notorious seat of Buddhist dissent which the government declared a national heritage site last month.
